cities.name: Kurukshetra
cities.overview: The land of the Mahabharata battle and the setting of the Bhagavad Gita, dotted with sacred tanks and temples.
cities.history: The land of the Mahabharata war and, according to Hindu tradition, the place where Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita. In the 7th century, it lay near Thanesar, capital of King Harsha.

cities.name: Gurugram
cities.overview: A fast-growing city south-west of Delhi, with a surprisingly good bird sanctuary on its rural edge.

cities.name: Pinjore
cities.overview: A town at the foot of the Shivalik hills in Panchkula district, about 20 km from Chandigarh.

cities.name: Faridabad
cities.overview: Haryana's most populous city, on the Delhi border, known for the Surajkund Crafts Mela.

cities.name: Panchkula
cities.overview: A planned city next to Chandigarh, the base for the Morni Hills.

cities.name: Yamunanagar
cities.overview: An industrial town on the Yamuna, close to the Kalesar forest.

cities.name: Hisar
cities.overview: A historic town in western Haryana, near the Harappan site at Rakhigarhi.

cities.name: Jhajjar
cities.overview: A town close to Delhi, known for its bird sanctuary at Bhindawas.

places.name: Brahma Sarovar
places.shortDescription: A vast sacred tank in Kurukshetra where pilgrims bathe, especially during solar eclipses and the Gita Jayanti festival.
places.description: Brahma Sarovar is one of the largest man-made water tanks in India, lined with ghats and temples, with a small shrine to Shiva on an island reached by a bridge. Hindus believe bathing here, particularly during a solar eclipse, brings great merit. A large bronze chariot of Krishna and Arjuna recalls the Bhagavad Gita. In late November or December the International Gita Mahotsav fills the ghats with lamps, crafts and performances.
places.history: Tradition links the tank to Brahma's creation of the world. Kurukshetra is named in the Mahabharata as the battlefield where Krishna delivered the Gita to Arjuna.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. The Gita Mahotsav is usually in late November or December.

places.name: Sultanpur National Park
places.shortDescription: A small wetland bird sanctuary near Gurugram where thousands of migratory birds spend the winter.
places.description: Sultanpur's shallow lake and surrounding scrub draw more than 250 bird species, among them painted storks, sarus cranes, flamingos, bar-headed geese and northern pintails that arrive from Central Asia and Siberia in winter. A walking trail circles the lake with watchtowers along the way. Arrive early in the morning with binoculars for the best sightings. It is an easy half-day trip from Delhi.
places.history: Ornithologist Peter Jackson and Salim Ali drew attention to the wetland in the 1960s. It became a bird sanctuary in 1972, a national park in 1989 and a Ramsar wetland of international importance in 2021.
places.bestTimeNote: November to March for migratory birds.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee for Indians and foreigners; extra for cameras.

location.address: Sultanpur, Farrukhnagar road, Gurugram district, Haryana 122506

places.name: Pinjore Gardens
places.shortDescription: A 17th-century Mughal terraced garden with fountains and palaces at the foot of the Shivalik hills.
places.description: The Yadavindra Gardens at Pinjore descend in seven terraces along a central water channel lined with fountains, cypresses and fruit trees. Small palaces in Rajasthani-Mughal style, such as the Sheesh Mahal and Rang Mahal, sit along the way. The fountains are lit up in the evenings, and the Pinjore Heritage Festival is held here in winter. It pairs well with a day in Chandigarh.
places.history: The garden was laid out in the 17th century by Nawab Fidai Khan, a foster brother of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. It later passed to the rulers of Patiala and was renamed after Maharaja Yadavindra Singh.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; evenings when the fountains are lit.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee charged by Haryana Tourism.

places.name: Jyotisar
places.shortDescription: The site at Kurukshetra where Krishna is said to have delivered the Bhagavad Gita under a banyan.
places.description: An old banyan beside a tank is said to be the descendant of the tree under which Krishna spoke. A sound and light show plays here in the evening.

places.name: Sheikh Chilli's Tomb
places.shortDescription: A Mughal-era tomb and madrasa at Thanesar, a building that some call the Taj of Haryana.
places.description: A marble-domed mausoleum for a Sufi, with a madrasa and a garden, near Harsh ka Tila, in the middle of the plains.

places.name: Surajkund
places.shortDescription: A 10th-century amphitheatre-shaped reservoir, home of a big international crafts fair each February.
places.description: A semi-circular stepped tank from the Tomar period, on the Delhi border. The Surajkund Mela draws craftspeople from across India and abroad.
places.history: Attributed to the Tomar king Surajpal in the 10th century.

places.name: Morni Hills
places.shortDescription: A small hill area in Panchkula, the only hill station in Haryana, with twin lakes and an old fort.
places.description: Forests and quiet hill roads, along with the Tikkar Taal lakes and a small fort museum. It's an easy day trip from Chandigarh.

places.name: Kalesar National Park
places.shortDescription: A sal forest in the Shivalik foothills of Yamunanagar, on the edge of Himachal and Uttarakhand.
places.description: A forest at the northern tip of Haryana, with leopards, elephants and a wide range of birds. It's quiet and still little visited.

places.name: Rakhigarhi
places.shortDescription: One of the largest Harappan sites known, in Hisar district, with ongoing excavations.
places.description: Low mounds that hide a huge Indus Valley city. Finds from here can be seen in a museum being developed on site.

places.name: Bhindawas Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A Ramsar-listed bird sanctuary in Jhajjar, close to Delhi, with big flocks in winter.
places.description: A wide wetland that fills with ducks and waders from November. It's among the closest good birding sites to Delhi.
